lyrics:
[Intro: warm soul guitar loop, vinyl crackle, slow drums]

[Refrain: low sung male voice, almost murmured]
Three a.m., the ceiling knows
Everything I don't let show
I lie here counting
The ceiling knows

[Verse 1: Southern male rap, slow and plain]
Heart going like I ran, and I ain't moved
Got a list in my head and it's all bad news
What if the plant shuts? What if the truck quits?
What if that cough the baby's got is something that sticks?
I check the locks twice, then I check 'em again
Stand in the hall like I'm waiting on a friend
My wife says, "Come to bed." I say, "I'm fine."
Been saying that since I was nine.

[Refrain: low sung male voice, almost murmured]
Three a.m., the ceiling knows
Everything I don't let show
I lie here counting
The ceiling knows

[Verse 2: rap, heavier, organ under]
My daddy never said a word about his nerves
He'd sit out on the porch and smoke and watch the curve
I thought that he was strong. I think he was scared.
I think nobody asked him, and nobody dared
At work I'm the one everybody leans on
Got jokes, got answers, got my game face on
Then I'm in the truck in the lot with my hands on my knees
Breathing like the doctor on the video. Lord, please.

[Verse 3: quieter, lighter]
Tuesday I told my brother on the phone
He said, "Man, me too. I thought I was alone."
We laughed till we coughed. Then he gave me a name.
A lady with an office. I went. No shame.
It ain't gone. I ain't fixed. That ain't how it goes.
But I slept six hours. And somebody knows.

[Final Refrain: sung, a second voice in harmony]
Three a.m., the ceiling knows
But I ain't the only one it's told
I said it out loud
Now somebody knows

[Outro: guitar loop, a long breath, a lamp clicked off]
producerBrief:
TEMPO / KEY / FEEL: 84 BPM, 4/4, E minor. Slow, warm and heavy-lidded, a late-night soul loop.

VOICE: Male, deep Texas drawl, rapped slowly and plainly with long pauses, as if talking to himself. The refrain is sung low and soft by the same man, and a second voice (his brother) harmonises on the last one.

INSTRUMENTS: A warm, clean soul guitar loop with a little wah, a slow, dusty drum break, a deep bass guitar, a Hammond organ from verse 2, soft strings, vinyl crackle.

ARRANGEMENT MAP: 0:00 Intro, guitar loop. 0:14 Refrain 1. 0:36 Verse 1. 1:20 Refrain 2. 1:42 Verse 2. 2:26 Verse 3, lighter. 3:00 Final refrain, in harmony. 3:28 Outro, a breath and a lamp, ends 3:56.

PRODUCTION & MIX: Early-1990s Houston rap: slow, bass-heavy and analogue, sampled soul warmth, vocals dry and close.

SIGNATURE MOMENT: 'He said, "Man, me too. I thought I was alone."' at 2:36.

MODERN POINT OF VIEW: The original admits the fear and stops there. Thirty-five years on, the song can go one step further: he tells his brother, and then a professional.

EMOTIONAL ARC: Racing, hiding, breaking the silence, resting.
